text: Fund managers are unlikely to escape bank based indirect supervision by terminating a lending relationship, because their dynamic trading strategies depend on the immediate availability of capital and lending relationships now face increased scrutiny.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Private Investment Fund Regulation - Theory and Empirical Evidence from 1998 to 2016 (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2998097

isBasedOn.name: Private Investment Fund Regulation - Theory and Empirical Evidence from 1998 to 2016

abstract: However, because private investment funds' dynamic trading strategies often depend on the immediate availability of capital, and given today's banking environment with increased scrutiny over lending and lending relationships, managers are unlikely to terminate a lending relationship.45

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: contemporary banking environment with heightened lending scrutiny
